195	class Standardiser:
196	    """Running per-column mean / std (Welford) over the rows processed so far; z of a new row uses the past rows only."""
197	
198	    def __init__(self, d, cols):
199	        self.n = np.zeros(d); self.mean = np.zeros(d); self.m2 = np.zeros(d); self.cols = np.asarray(cols, dtype=int)
200	
201	    def transform(self, x):
202	        z = x.copy()
203	        c = self.cols
204	        v = x[c]; miss = np.isnan(v)
205	        n = self.n[c]; sd = np.sqrt(np.where(n > 1, self.m2[c] / np.maximum(n - 1, 1), 0.0))
206	        ok = (n >= 2) & (sd > 1e-12) & ~miss
207	        out = np.zeros(len(c))
208	        out[ok] = np.clip((v[ok] - self.mean[c][ok]) / sd[ok], -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP)
209	        z[c] = out
210	        return z
211	
212	    def update(self, x):
213	        c = self.cols; v = x[c]; ok = ~np.isnan(v)
214	        idx = c[ok]; val = v[ok]
215	        self.n[idx] += 1
216	        delta = val - self.mean[idx]
217	        self.mean[idx] += delta / self.n[idx]
218	        self.m2[idx] += delta * (val - self.mean[idx])

224	    (vectorised over an array of nets)."""

233	def kelly_lots(p, W, L, sz):
234	    """Half-Kelly lots for a bet paying b = W / L to 1: f* = p - (1 - p) / b, f = fraction x f*, lots = clip(floor(f x capital / L), 0, max)."""
235	    if W is None and L is None: return 1, None
236	    if W is None: W = L
237	    if L is None or L <= 0: L = W
238	    if W <= 0 or L <= 0: return 0, 0.0
239	    b = W / L
240	    f_star = p - (1.0 - p) / b
241	    f = sz["fraction"] * f_star
242	    lots = int(np.clip(math.floor(f * sz["capital_inr"] / L), 0, sz["max_lots"])) if f > 0 else 0
243	    return lots, float(f)

246	class Record:
247	    """The walk-forward record of (score at decision time, net, win) of the closed SETUPs: calibration and the nested tau."""
248	
249	    def __init__(self, cal, tau_rule):
250	        self.scores, self.nets, self.wins = [], [], []
251	        self.cal, self.tau_rule = cal, tau_rule
252	        self.n_win = 0; self.sum_win = 0.0; self.n_loss = 0; self.sum_loss = 0.0
253	
254	    def add(self, score, net):
255	        self.scores.append(score); self.nets.append(net); self.wins.append(net > 0)
256	        if net > 0: self.n_win += 1; self.sum_win += net
257	        else: self.n_loss += 1; self.sum_loss += -net
258	
259	    def W(self): return self.sum_win / self.n_win if self.n_win else None
260	
261	    def L(self): return self.sum_loss / self.n_loss if self.n_loss else None
262	
263	    def p_cal(self, score):
264	        n = len(self.scores)
265	        if n == 0 or score is None or not np.isfinite(score): return 0.5
266	        base = float(np.mean(self.wins))
267	        if n < self.cal["min_record"]: return base
268	        s = np.asarray(self.scores); w = np.asarray(self.wins, dtype=float)
269	        edges = np.quantile(s, np.linspace(0, 1, self.cal["bins"] + 1)[1:-1])
270	        b = int(np.searchsorted(edges, score, side="right")); bins = np.searchsorted(edges, s, side="right")
271	        m = bins == b
272	        return float(w[m].mean()) if m.sum() >= self.cal["min_bin"] else base
273	
274	    def tau(self, reward, ru):
275	        r = self.tau_rule
276	        if len(self.scores) < r["min_record"]: return r["fallback"], "fallback"
277	        s = np.asarray(self.scores); pn = np.asarray([penalised_net(v, reward, ru) for v in self.nets])
278	        g0, g1, st = r["grid"]; grid = np.round(np.arange(g0, g1 + st / 2, st), 4)
279	        best, best_v = None, -np.inf
280	        for t in grid:
281	            k = s >= t
282	            if k.sum() < r["kept_n_min"] or k.mean() < r["kept_share_min"]: continue
283	            v = float(pn[k].mean())
284	            if v > best_v: best, best_v = float(t), v
285	        return (best, "record") if best is not None else (r["fallback"], "fallback")

292	class LinTS:
293	    """rl.LinTS's arm model for the single arm `take` (skip = 0), refitted from the window."""
294	
295	    def __init__(self, d, ridge):
296	        self.d, self.ridge = d, ridge
297	        self.A = np.eye(d) * ridge; self.b = np.zeros(d); self.mu = np.zeros(d); self.chol = np.linalg.cholesky(np.eye(d) / ridge); self.n = 0
298	
299	    def refit(self, X, r, y, w):
300	        """Recompute A, b from the window (the rolling windows)."""
301	        self.set_sums(np.eye(self.d) * self.ridge + X.T @ X, X.T @ r, len(r))
302	
303	    def set_sums(self, A, b, n):
304	        """A = ridge I + sum x x', b = sum r x (the anchored window accumulates them exactly, one batch of closed outcomes at
305	        a time, instead of recomputing X'X over every closed row at every refit: the same estimator, O(d^2) per outcome)."""
306	        self.A = A; self.b = b
307	        self.mu = np.linalg.solve(self.A, self.b)
308	        Ainv = np.linalg.inv(self.A); Ainv = (Ainv + Ainv.T) / 2
309	        self.chol = np.linalg.cholesky(Ainv + 1e-12 * np.eye(self.d)); self.n = n
310	
311	    def score(self, x): return float(x @ self.mu)
312	
313	    def decide(self, x, score, head, z, W, L, ru):
314	        if head["explore"] > 0:
315	            v = float(x @ (self.mu + head["explore"] * (self.chol @ z)))
316	            return v > 0, ("TS sample > 0" if v > 0 else "TS sample <= 0"), v
317	        return score > 0, ("posterior mean > 0" if score > 0 else "posterior mean <= 0"), score
318	
319	    def state_id(self, n_applied): return _sha(self.A.tobytes() + self.b.tobytes() + str(n_applied).encode())

322	class LogTS:
323	    """Bayesian logistic regression (Laplace) of the win label; decision by expected net p W - (1 - p) L."""
324	
325	    def __init__(self, d, ridge, newton):
326	        self.d, self.ridge, self.newton = d, ridge, newton
327	        self.w = np.zeros(d); self.chol = np.linalg.cholesky(np.eye(d) / ridge); self.n = 0; self.steps = 0
328	
329	    def refit(self, X, r, y, w):
330	        wv = self.w.copy(); ridge = self.ridge; I = np.eye(self.d)
331	        for it in range(self.newton["max_steps"]):
332	            p = _sigmoid(X @ wv)
333	            g = X.T @ (p - y) + ridge * wv
334	            Hm = (X * (p * (1 - p))[:, None]).T @ X + ridge * I
335	            step = np.linalg.solve(Hm, g)
336	            wv = wv - step
337	            self.steps = it + 1
338	            if np.max(np.abs(step)) < self.newton["tol"]: break
339	        p = _sigmoid(X @ wv)
340	        Hm = (X * (p * (1 - p))[:, None]).T @ X + ridge * I
341	        Hinv = np.linalg.inv(Hm); Hinv = (Hinv + Hinv.T) / 2
342	        self.w = wv; self.chol = np.linalg.cholesky(Hinv + 1e-12 * I); self.n = len(y)
343	
344	    def score(self, x): return float(_sigmoid(x @ self.w))
345	
346	    def decide(self, x, score, head, z, W, L, ru):
347	        p = float(_sigmoid(x @ (self.w + head["explore"] * (self.chol @ z)))) if head["explore"] > 0 else score
348	        if W is None and L is None: return True, "no closed outcome with a sign yet: take", None
349	        Wv = W if W is not None else L; Lv = L if L is not None else Wv
350	        Lp = Lv * ru["pf_loss_mult"] if head["reward"] == "pf" else Lv
351	        e = p * Wv - (1 - p) * Lp
352	        return e > 0, ("pW-(1-p)L > 0" if e > 0 else "pW-(1-p)L <= 0"), float(e)
353	
354	    def state_id(self, n_applied): return _sha(self.w.tobytes() + str(n_applied).encode())

357	class HGB:
358	    """HistGradientBoosting regressor (winsorised net) or classifier (win label, |net| weights, nested tau)."""
359	
360	    def __init__(self, kind, params, seed, reward, ru, tau_rule):
361	        self.kind, self.params, self.seed, self.reward, self.ru = kind, dict(params), seed, reward, ru
362	        self.model = None; self.n = 0; self._sid = None
363	        # the classifier's nested tau, one per decision-side reward (the `pf` head chooses tau on the record's penalised net,
364	        # the `net` head on the net: the reward enters the DECISION for the win-label learners)
365	        self.taus = {r: (tau_rule["fallback"], "fallback") for r in ("net", "pf")}
366	
367	    def refit(self, X, r, y, w, record=None):
368	        P = dict(self.params, early_stopping=False, random_state=self.seed)
369	        if self.kind == "reg":
370	            lo, hi = np.quantile(r, [0.01, 0.99])
371	            t = np.clip(r, lo, hi)
372	            if self.reward == "pf": t = np.where(t < 0, t * self.ru["pf_loss_mult"], t)
373	            self.model = HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss="squared_error", **P).fit(X, t)
374	        else:
375	            a = np.abs(r); cap = np.quantile(a, 0.99); sw = np.minimum(a, cap); sw = sw / sw.mean() if sw.mean() > 0 else np.ones_like(sw)
376	            if y.min() == y.max():
377	                self.model = None; self.const = float(y[0])
378	            else:
379	                self.model = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(class_weight="balanced", **P).fit(X, y.astype(int), sample_weight=sw)
380	            if record is not None: self.taus = {rw: record.tau(rw, self.ru) for rw in ("net", "pf")}
381	        self.n = len(r); self._sid = _sha(pickle.dumps(self.model) + str(self.n).encode())
382	
383	    def tau_for(self, head_reward):
384	        return self.taus[head_reward if head_reward in self.taus else "net"]
385	
386	    def score(self, x):
387	        if self.model is None: return 0.0 if self.kind == "reg" else getattr(self, "const", 0.5)
388	        if self.kind == "reg": return float(self.model.predict(x[None, :])[0])
389	        return float(self.model.predict_proba(x[None, :])[0, 1])
390	
391	    def decide(self, x, score, head, z, W, L, ru):
392	        if self.kind == "reg": return score > 0, ("E[net] > 0" if score > 0 else "E[net] <= 0"), score
393	        tau, src = self.tau_for(head["reward"])
394	        return score >= tau, (f"p >= tau ({src}, {head['reward']})" if score >= tau else f"p < tau ({src}, {head['reward']})"), score
395	
396	    def state_id(self, n_applied): return self._sid or "prior:0"

401	    if cfg["learner"] == "logts": return LogTS(d, cfg["ridge"], cfg["newton"])
402	    return HGB("reg" if cfg["learner"] == "hgb_reg" else "cls", cfg["hgb"], cfg["seed"], cfg["reward"], cfg["reward_unit"], cfg["tau_rule"])

406	def run_heads(T, cfg, rows, heads, features_out=None):
407	    """One fit sequence, several decision heads. heads: list of {explore, seed, reward}. Returns {head index: dict(decisions,
408	    journal, states)}; features_out (list) receives the standardised feature vector of every row when given."""
409	    cfg = with_defaults(cfg)
410	    rows = np.asarray(rows, dtype=int)
411	    if len(rows) > 1 and not (np.diff(T.setup_i[rows]) > 0).all(): raise ValueError("rows must be strictly increasing in setup_i (time order)")
412	    spec = cfg["encoded"] if cfg.get("encoded") else design_spec(T, cfg["design"])
413	    with threadpool_limits(limits=1):
414	        return _walk(T, cfg, rows, heads, spec, features_out)

417	def _walk(T, cfg, rows, heads, spec, features_out):
418	    F = T.F
419	    Xraw = encode(T, spec, rows)
420	    kinds = [e["kind"] for e in spec]
421	    std_cols = [j for j, k in enumerate(kinds) if cfg["design"] == "full" and k in ("num", "bool")]
422	    d = len(spec) + 1
423	    std = Standardiser(len(spec), std_cols)
424	    ru, sz, k_cad, win = cfg["reward_unit"], cfg["sizing"], cfg["cadence_k"], cfg["window"]
425	    learner = make_learner(cfg, d)
426	    record = Record(cfg["calibration"], cfg["tau_rule"])
427	    setup_i = T.setup_i[rows]; exit_bar = T.exit_bar[rows]; net_all = T.net[rows]
428	    col = lambda c: F[c].iloc[rows].to_numpy() if c in F.columns else np.array([None] * len(rows))
429	    time_ = col("time").astype(str); dir_ = col("dir").astype(str); hb = col("hour_bin").astype(str); ses = T.session[rows]
430	    fill = col("close"); sl_dist = col("sl_dist_pts"); x_time = col("l1_exit_time"); x_reason = col("l1_exit_reason")
431	    mfe = col("l1_mfe_pts"); mae = col("l1_mae_pts"); pts = col("l1_pts"); gross = col("l1_gross_inr"); cost = col("l1_cost_inr")
432	    n = len(rows)
433	    Xs = np.zeros((n, d)); scores = np.full(n, np.nan)
434	    queue, pending, closed = [], [], []                    # closed = indices (into rows) of every closed outcome in exit order
435	    n_applied = 0; state_id = "prior:0"
436	    A_acc = np.eye(d) * cfg["ridge"]; b_acc = np.zeros(d)   # the anchored lints sums (exact accumulation)
437	    hs = []
438	    for h in heads:
439	        hs.append(dict(rng=np.random.RandomState(int(h["seed"])), explore=float(h["explore"]), reward=h.get("reward", cfg["reward"]),
440	                       book=[], eq1=0.0, eqs=0.0, pk1=0.0, pks=0.0, last100=[], n_taken_closed=0, today=None, today_net=0.0,
441	                       decisions=[], journal=[], states=[]))
442	    for i in range(n):
443	        k = int(setup_i[i])
444	        # 1. outcomes whose exit bar is before this bar become known (rl.walk: the queue is popped by exit time)
445	        while queue and queue[0][0] < k:
446	            _, j = heapq.heappop(queue)
447	            record.add(scores[j], float(net_all[j])); closed.append(j); pending.append(j)
448	            if len(pending) >= k_cad:
449	                sel = closed if win == "anchored" else closed[-int(win):]
450	                if cfg["learner"] == "lints" and win == "anchored":
451	                    Xp = Xs[pending]; rp = fit_reward(net_all[pending], cfg["reward"], ru)
452	                    A_acc = A_acc + Xp.T @ Xp; b_acc = b_acc + Xp.T @ rp
453	                    learner.set_sums(A_acc, b_acc, len(closed))
454	                else:
455	                    Xw = Xs[sel]; nets = net_all[sel].astype(float)
456	                    y = (nets > 0).astype(float)
457	                    if isinstance(learner, HGB): learner.refit(Xw, nets, y, None, record=record)
458	                    elif cfg["learner"] == "lints": learner.refit(Xw, fit_reward(nets, cfg["reward"], ru), y, None)
459	                    else: learner.refit(Xw, nets, y, None)
460	                n_applied += len(pending); pending = []
461	                state_id = learner.state_id(n_applied)
462	        for h in hs:
463	            while h["book"] and h["book"][0][0] < k:
464	                _, j, lots = heapq.heappop(h["book"])
465	                nv = float(net_all[j]); h["eq1"] += nv; h["eqs"] += nv * lots
466	                h["pk1"] = max(h["pk1"], h["eq1"]); h["pks"] = max(h["pks"], h["eqs"])
467	                h["last100"].append(nv); h["last100"] = h["last100"][-100:]; h["n_taken_closed"] += 1
468	                day = str(time_[j])[:10]
469	                if h["today"] != str(time_[i])[:10]: h["today"], h["today_net"] = str(time_[i])[:10], 0.0
470	                if day == h["today"]: h["today_net"] += nv * lots
471	        # 2. the feature vector (past-only standardisation), the model score, the calibrated p_win
472	        x = np.append(std.transform(Xraw[i]), 1.0); Xs[i] = x
473	        if features_out is not None: features_out.append(x)
474	        sc = learner.score(x); scores[i] = sc
475	        p_cal = record.p_cal(sc); W, L = record.W(), record.L()
476	        warm = n_applied < cfg["warmup_min_closed"]
477	        # 3. every head decides (one normal vector per head per SETUP, drawn whatever happens)
478	        for h in hs:
479	            z = h["rng"].standard_normal(d)
480	            if h["today"] != str(time_[i])[:10]: h["today"], h["today_net"] = str(time_[i])[:10], 0.0
481	            if warm:
482	                take, reason, val = (cfg["warmup_policy"] == "take"), f"warm-up (< {cfg['warmup_min_closed']} closed): {cfg['warmup_policy']}-all", None
483	                lots, f = (1, None) if take else (0, None)
484	            else:
485	                take, reason, val = learner.decide(x, sc, h, z, W, L, ru)
486	                if take and sz.get("daily_loss_stop") is not None and h["today_net"] <= -float(sz["daily_loss_stop"]):
487	                    take, reason = False, f"daily loss stop {sz['daily_loss_stop']}"
488	                lots, f = kelly_lots(p_cal, W, L, sz) if take else (0, None)
489	            tau = learner.tau_for(h["reward"])[0] if isinstance(learner, HGB) and learner.kind == "cls" else None
490	            wl = [] if h["last100"] == [] else h["last100"]
491	            gw = sum(v for v in wl if v > 0); gl = -sum(v for v in wl if v <= 0)
492	            pf100 = round(gw / gl, 3) if gl > 0 else None
493	            nv = float(net_all[i])
494	            R = nv / (float(sl_dist[i]) * LOT) if sl_dist[i] is not None and np.isfinite(float(sl_dist[i])) and float(sl_dist[i]) > 0 else None
495	            feat = json.dumps([round(float(v), 6) for v in x]) if cfg["design"] == "context" else f"ref:{i}|sha:{_sha(x.tobytes())}"
496	            h["decisions"].append(dict(take=bool(take), lots=int(lots), score=None if sc is None else round(float(sc), 6), p_win=round(float(p_cal), 4),
497	                                       reason=reason, state=state_id))
498	            h["states"].append(state_id)
499	            h["journal"].append(dict(
500	                time=str(time_[i]), setup_i=k, session_idx=int(ses[i]), dir=str(dir_[i]), hour_bin=str(hb[i]), features=feat,
501	                n_closed=int(n_applied), n_pending=int(len(pending)), decision="take" if take else "skip", reason=reason,
502	                score=round(float(sc), 6), value=None if val is None else round(float(val), 6),
503	                p_model=round(float(sc), 6) if cfg["learner"] in ("logts", "hgb_cls") else None, p_win=round(float(p_cal), 4), tau=tau,
504	                W=None if W is None else round(W, 2), L=None if L is None else round(L, 2), kelly_f=None if f is None else round(f, 5), lots=int(lots),
505	                state=state_id, fill=None if fill[i] is None else float(fill[i]), exit_time=None if x_time[i] is None else str(x_time[i]),
506	                exit_reason=None if x_reason[i] is None else str(x_reason[i]), mfe_pts=_f(mfe[i]), mae_pts=_f(mae[i]), pts=_f(pts[i]),
507	                gross=_f(gross[i]), costs=_f(cost[i]), net=round(nv, 2), R=None if R is None else round(R, 4),
508	                equity_1lot=round(h["eq1"], 2), drawdown_1lot=round(h["eq1"] - h["pk1"], 2), equity_sized=round(h["eqs"], 2),
509	                drawdown_sized=round(h["eqs"] - h["pks"], 2), rolling_pf100=pf100, n_taken_closed=int(h["n_taken_closed"]),
510	                taken_net=round(nv * lots, 2) if take else 0.0))
511	            if take: heapq.heappush(h["book"], (int(exit_bar[i]), i, int(lots)))
512	        # 4. this SETUP's outcome joins the queue (known at its exit bar); the standardiser learns this row's features
513	        heapq.heappush(queue, (int(exit_bar[i]), i))
514	        std.update(Xraw[i])
515	    return {hi: dict(decisions=h["decisions"], journal=h["journal"], states=h["states"]) for hi, h in enumerate(hs)}

1	"""run_online.py - the driver of study online_learner for one timeframe (IS rows, label L1, time order).
2	
3	    python run_online.py --tf 5minute --workers 2 --stage all       # spec, fit, score, checks
4	    python run_online.py --tf minute --stage fit                    # one stage; every stage is resumable (checkpoints)
5	
6	Stages
7	  spec    the two designs' encoded column lists from the real IS rows (results/<tf>/spec_<design>.json).
8	  fit     every fit sequence (job) = (design, learner, cadence_k, window, fit reward) with its decision heads (explore x seed x
9	          decision-side reward), run by online.run_heads in parallel worker processes (one BLAS thread each); per job a
10	          checkpoint results/<tf>/jobs/<job>.pkl (keep / lots arrays, state ids, per-head cfg) and the journal
11	          results/<tf>/journals/<job>.parquet (one row per SETUP per head). The full design's standardised feature vectors are
12	          written once (results/<tf>/features_full.parquet) and every full job's vectors are asserted identical to them.
13	  score   every head = one harness.score row (family online/<design>/<learner>/k<k>/<window>/<reward>, config = the cfg with
14	          explore / seed; controls 2,000 draws) appended to results/<tf>/scores.jsonl, plus the cheap learning curve every 250
15	          SETUPs (harness.metrics without controls on the prefix rows) in results/<tf>/curves.jsonl; the comparators take-all and
16	          the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as rows of family online_comparator/<name> (excluded from the online family's PBO / SPA).
17	  checks  determinism (a fresh double run of a fixed subset of jobs; journal sha, decisions and state ids must be identical, and
18	          equal to the fit stage's stored decisions) and truncation (the run on the rows before 2025-06-30 12:00 and the run on
19	          data/<tf>/trunc_20250630_120000 must give the same decisions for every SETUP before the cut): results/<tf>/checks.json.

132	def stage_spec(tf):
133	    T = table(tf); os.makedirs(os.path.join(RES, tf), exist_ok=True)
134	    for design in O.DESIGNS:
135	        spec = O.design_spec(T, design)
136	        json.dump(spec, open(spec_path(tf, design), "w"), indent=0)
137	        print(f"[{tf}] spec {design}: {len(spec)} encoded columns from {len({e['source'] for e in spec})} source columns "
138	              f"(time proxies excluded: {sorted(H.TIME_PROXIES)}); sha {spec_sha(spec)}", flush=True)
139	
140	
141	def stage_fit(tf, workers):
142	    from joblib import Parallel, delayed
143	    specs = {d: load_spec(tf, d) for d in O.DESIGNS}
144	    todo = [j for j in jobs(tf) if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(RES, tf, "jobs", j["id"] + ".pkl"))]
145	    print(f"[{tf}] fit: {len(jobs(tf))} jobs, {len(todo)} to run, workers {workers}", flush=True)
146	    # the expensive ones first so the pool stays busy
147	    cost = lambda j: (0 if j["cfg"]["design"] == "full" else 1, j["cfg"]["cadence_k"], 0 if j["cfg"]["learner"] in ("logts", "hgb_reg", "hgb_cls") else 1)
148	    todo.sort(key=cost)
149	    t0 = time.time()
150	    for r in Parallel(n_jobs=workers, backend="loky", return_as="generator")(delayed(run_job)(tf, j, specs[j["cfg"]["design"]]) for j in todo):
151	        print(f"[{tf}] job {r['id']:<48} {r['seconds']:8.1f}s heads {r['heads']} features_sha {r['features_sha']}  ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s elapsed)", flush=True)
152	    shas = {p["features_sha"] for p in (pickle.load(open(os.path.join(RES, tf, "jobs", j["id"] + ".pkl"), "rb")) for j in jobs(tf) if j["cfg"]["design"] == "full")}
153	    print(f"[{tf}] full-design feature vectors identical across jobs: {len(shas) == 1} {sorted(shas)}", flush=True)
154	
155	
156	def curve(T, keep, rows, lots=None):
157	    out = []
158	    n = len(rows); pts = list(range(CURVE_STEP, n, CURVE_STEP)) + [n]
159	    net = T.net
160	    for m in pts:
161	        r = rows[:m]; mt = H.metrics(T, keep, r, "", controls=False)
162	        row = dict(n=m, kept_n=mt["kept_n"], kept_share=mt["kept_share"], diff=mt["diff"], kept_mean=mt["kept_mean"], kept_pf=mt["kept_pf"],
163	                   kept_sum=round(float(net[r][keep[r]].sum()), 2), all_sum=round(float(net[r].sum()), 2), sign_blocks=mt["sign_blocks"])
164	        if lots is not None: row["sized_sum"] = round(float((net[r] * lots[:m] * keep[r]).sum()), 2)
165	        out.append(row)
166	    return out
167	
168	
169	def stage_score(tf):
170	    T = table(tf); rows = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
171	    sp = os.path.join(RES, tf, "scores.jsonl"); cp = os.path.join(RES, tf, "curves.jsonl")
172	    done = {json.loads(l)["id"] for l in open(sp, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()} if os.path.exists(sp) else set()
173	    n_new = 0; t0 = time.time()
174	    for j in jobs(tf):
175	        p = os.path.join(RES, tf, "jobs", j["id"] + ".pkl")
176	        if not os.path.exists(p): print(f"[{tf}] score: job {j['id']} missing, skipped", flush=True); continue
177	        J = pickle.load(open(p, "rb"))
178	        for h in J["heads"]:
179	            c = h["cfg_ledger"]; fam = family(c)
180	            cid = H.candidate_id(fam, c, T.label, T.tf)
181	            if cid in done: continue
182	            keep = np.zeros(T.n, dtype=bool); keep[rows] = h["keep"]
183	            res = H.score(T, keep, fam, c, script=__file__)
184	            res["job"] = j["id"]; res["head"] = h["head"]; res["journal_sha"] = h["journal_sha"]
185	            res["lots_mean_taken"] = round(float(h["lots"][h["keep"]].mean()), 3) if h["keep"].any() else None
186	            res["take_and_zero_lots"] = int(((h["lots"] == 0) & h["keep"]).sum())
187	            res["sized_net"] = round(float((T.net[rows] * h["lots"] * h["keep"]).sum()), 2)
188	            w = T.net[rows] * h["lots"] * h["keep"]; gw, gl = w[w > 0].sum(), -w[w < 0].sum()
189	            res["sized_pf"] = round(float(gw / gl), 3) if gl > 0 else None
190	            with open(sp, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(json.dumps(res, default=str) + "\n")
191	            with open(cp, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(json.dumps(dict(id=res["id"], family=fam, curve=curve(T, keep, rows, h["lots"]))) + "\n")
192	            done.add(cid); n_new += 1
193	            if n_new % 20 == 0: print(f"[{tf}] scored {n_new} rows ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
194	    # comparators (own family, outside online/*)
195	    comps = {"take_all": (np.ones(T.n, dtype=bool), "pre_registration.json"), "frozen_st7_st8": (T.F.fz_traded.astype(bool).to_numpy(), "pre_registration.json")}
196	    # the gate_family study's OOF decisions (studies/gate_family/results/oof_<tf>_<sub>.parquet: one row per sub-family x model x IS
197	    # unit, columns setup_i, sub, model, keep): the sub-family's finalist model when gate_family/findings.json names one, else every
198	    # model in the file (labelled by sub / model; the h5_full sub is outside the frozen shortlist). Absent files are recorded.
199	    gf_dir = os.path.join(OUT, "studies", "gate_family"); gf_files = []
200	    fj = os.path.join(gf_dir, "findings.json"); fin = json.load(open(fj)).get("timeframes", {}).get(tf, {}).get("sub_families", {}) if os.path.exists(fj) else {}
201	    for sub in ("context", "h5_full"):
202	        gf = os.path.join(gf_dir, "results", f"oof_{tf}_{sub}.parquet")
203	        if not os.path.exists(gf): continue
204	        gf_files.append(os.path.relpath(gf, OUT)); G = pd.read_parquet(gf)
205	        fm = ((fin.get(sub) or {}).get("finalist") or {}).get("model")
206	        models = [fm] if fm and fm in set(G.model) else sorted(set(G.model))
207	        for mdl in models:
208	            m = dict(zip(G.setup_i[G.model == mdl], G.keep[G.model == mdl].astype(bool)))
209	            comps[f"gate_family_oof/{sub}/{mdl}" + ("/finalist" if fm == mdl else "")] = (np.array([bool(m.get(int(s), True)) for s in T.setup_i]), os.path.relpath(gf, OUT))
210	    for name, (keep, src) in comps.items():
211	        fam = f"online_comparator/{name}"; c = dict(comparator=name, source=src)
212	        if name.startswith("gate_family_oof/h5_full"): c["vocabulary"] = "outside the frozen shortlist"
213	        if H.candidate_id(fam, c, T.label, T.tf) in done: continue
214	        res = H.score(T, keep, fam, c, script=__file__); res["job"] = "comparator"; res["head"] = None
215	        with open(sp, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(json.dumps(res, default=str) + "\n")
216	        with open(cp, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(json.dumps(dict(id=res["id"], family=fam, curve=curve(T, keep, rows))) + "\n")
217	        done.add(res["id"])
218	    print(f"[{tf}] score: {n_new} new rows, gate_family OOF files {gf_files or 'absent'} ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
219	
220	
221	CHECK_JOBS = {  # design, learner, k, window, fit reward: the fixed subset the determinism / truncation checks run on
222	    "context": [("lints", 1, "anchored", "net"), ("lints", 10, 300, "pf"), ("lints", 50, 1000, "net"), ("logts", 1, "anchored", None), ("logts", 10, 300, None),
223	                ("logts", 50, 1000, None), ("hgb_reg", 50, "anchored", "net"), ("hgb_cls", 50, 1000, None)],
224	    "full": [("lints", 10, 1000, "net"), ("logts", 50, "anchored", None)]}
225	
226	
227	def stage_checks(tf):
228	    T = table(tf); rows = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
229	    specs = {d: load_spec(tf, d) for d in O.DESIGNS}
230	    tfold = os.path.join(OUT, "data", tf, "trunc_20250630_120000")
231	    Ttr = O.load_table(tfold, tf)
232	    time_full = T.F.time.astype(str).to_numpy(); time_tr = Ttr.F.time.astype(str).to_numpy()
233	    rows_cut = rows[time_full[rows] < O.CUT]
234	    rows_tr = np.flatnonzero(Ttr.is_mask); rows_tr = rows_tr[time_tr[rows_tr] < O.CUT]
235	    common = sorted(set(T.setup_i[rows_cut].tolist()) & set(Ttr.setup_i[rows_tr].tolist()))
236	    # label sanity: trades closed before the cut bar carry the same net in both builds
237	    cut_bar = int(T.F.setup_i[time_full >= O.CUT].min()) if (time_full >= O.CUT).any() else int(T.setup_i.max()) + 1
238	    nf = dict(zip(T.setup_i, T.net)); nt = dict(zip(Ttr.setup_i, Ttr.net)); xb = dict(zip(T.setup_i, T.exit_bar))
239	    closed_before = [s for s in common if xb[s] < cut_bar]
240	    label_same = all(abs(nf[s] - nt[s]) < 0.005 for s in closed_before)
241	    out = dict(tf=tf, cut=O.CUT, rows_is=int(len(rows)), rows_before_cut=int(len(rows_cut)), trunc_rows_before_cut=int(len(rows_tr)), common_setups=len(common),
242	               closed_before_cut=len(closed_before), labels_identical_closed_before_cut=bool(label_same), jobs=[])
243	    print(f"[{tf}] checks: {len(rows_cut)} rows before the cut, trunc build {len(rows_tr)}, common {len(common)}, labels identical on closed trades: {label_same}", flush=True)
244	    for design, lst in CHECK_JOBS.items():
245	        for learner, k, window, fr in lst:
246	            jid = job_id(design, learner, k, window, fr)
247	            J = pickle.load(open(os.path.join(RES, tf, "jobs", jid + ".pkl"), "rb"))
248	            heads = [J["heads"][0]["head"]] + ([h["head"] for h in J["heads"] if h["head"]["explore"] > 0][:1])
249	            cfgj = dict(J["cfg"], encoded=specs[design], columns=sorted({e["source"] for e in specs[design]}))
250	            t0 = time.time()
251	            r1 = O.run_heads(T, cfgj, rows, heads); r2 = O.run_heads(T, cfgj, rows, heads)
252	            rc = O.run_heads(T, cfgj, rows_cut, heads); rt = O.run_heads(Ttr, cfgj, rows_tr, heads)
253	            rec = dict(job=jid, heads=heads, seconds=round(time.time() - t0, 1))
254	            for hi, h in enumerate(heads):
255	                stored = next(x for x in J["heads"] if x["head"] == h)
256	                d1 = [d["take"] for d in r1[hi]["decisions"]]; d2 = [d["take"] for d in r2[hi]["decisions"]]
257	                det = (O.journal_sha(r1[hi]["journal"]) == O.journal_sha(r2[hi]["journal"]) and r1[hi]["decisions"] == r2[hi]["decisions"] and r1[hi]["states"] == r2[hi]["states"])
258	                same_as_stored = (d1 == stored["keep"].tolist()) and (O.journal_sha(r1[hi]["journal"]) == stored["journal_sha"])
259	                m = len(rows_cut)
260	                trunc_a = r1[hi]["decisions"][:m] == rc[hi]["decisions"] and r1[hi]["states"][:m] == rc[hi]["states"]
261	                dfull = dict(zip(T.setup_i[rows_cut].tolist(), (d["take"] for d in r1[hi]["decisions"][:m])))
262	                dtr = dict(zip(Ttr.setup_i[rows_tr].tolist(), (d["take"] for d in rt[hi]["decisions"])))
263	                lfull = dict(zip(T.setup_i[rows_cut].tolist(), (d["lots"] for d in r1[hi]["decisions"][:m])))
264	                ltr = dict(zip(Ttr.setup_i[rows_tr].tolist(), (d["lots"] for d in rt[hi]["decisions"])))
265	                trunc_b = all(dfull[s] == dtr[s] and lfull[s] == ltr[s] for s in common)
266	                rec[f"head_{hi}"] = dict(head=h, deterministic=bool(det), equals_stored=bool(same_as_stored), truncation_prefix_identical=bool(trunc_a),
267	                                         truncation_build_identical=bool(trunc_b), n_compared=len(common), decisions_differ=int(sum(dfull[s] != dtr[s] for s in common)))
268	                print(f"[{tf}]  {jid} head {h}: deterministic {det}, = stored {same_as_stored}, prefix {trunc_a}, trunc build {trunc_b} ({rec['seconds']}s)", flush=True)
269	            out["jobs"].append(rec)
270	    out["all_pass"] = bool(label_same and all(v["deterministic"] and v["equals_stored"] and v["truncation_prefix_identical"] and v["truncation_build_identical"]
271	                                             for j in out["jobs"] for kk, v in j.items() if kk.startswith("head_")))
272	    json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(RES, tf, "checks.json"), "w"), indent=1, default=str)
273	    print(f"[{tf}] checks all pass: {out['all_pass']}", flush=True)
274	
275	
276	if __name__ == "__main__":
277	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument("--tf", required=True); ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=2)
278	    ap.add_argument("--stage", default="all", choices=["spec", "fit", "score", "checks", "all"]); a = ap.parse_args()
279	    t0 = time.time(); print(f"[{a.tf}] start {D.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')} stage {a.stage}", flush=True)
280	    if a.stage in ("spec", "all"): stage_spec(a.tf)
281	    if a.stage in ("fit", "all"): stage_fit(a.tf, a.workers)
282	    if a.stage in ("score", "all"): stage_score(a.tf)
283	    if a.stage in ("checks", "all"): stage_checks(a.tf)
284	    print(f"[{a.tf}] done in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s; ledger sha {H.ledger_sha()}", flush=True)

366	def pbo(vectors, statistic="kept_mean", S=CSCV_S):
367	    """CSCV probability of backtest overfitting (Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado & Zhu 2017) over a family of candidates.
368	    vectors: list of session_vectors dicts (one per candidate, same sessions). Each candidate's per-session series is split into
369	    S contiguous blocks; for every C(S, S/2) partition the IS-best candidate's OOS rank is recorded; PBO = share of partitions
370	    where that rank is below the median (logit < 0). statistic: 'kept_mean' = kept net per kept trade over the half, or 'diff'
371	    = kept mean minus skipped mean over the half. Also the IS-vs-OOS performance degradation slope and the share of partitions
372	    where the IS-best is below zero OOS."""
373	    M = len(vectors)
374	    if M < 2: return dict(candidates=M, pbo=None, note="needs at least 2 candidates")
375	    T_ = len(vectors[0]["sessions"]); edges = np.linspace(0, T_, S + 1).round().astype(int)
376	    def blocks(v, key):
377	        return np.array([v[key][edges[b]:edges[b + 1]].sum() for b in range(S)])
378	    KS = np.array([blocks(v, "kept_sum") for v in vectors]); KN = np.array([blocks(v, "kept_n") for v in vectors])
379	    SS = np.array([blocks(v, "skipped_sum") for v in vectors]); SN = np.array([blocks(v, "skipped_n") for v in vectors])
380	    P = _partitions(S).astype(float)                                           # partitions x S
381	    def perf(Pm):
382	        ks, kn = Pm @ KS.T, Pm @ KN.T                                           # partitions x M
383	        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
384	            km = np.where(kn > 0, ks / kn, np.nan)
385	            if statistic == "kept_mean": return km
386	            ss, sn = Pm @ SS.T, Pm @ SN.T
387	            return km - np.where(sn > 0, ss / sn, np.nan)
388	    ins, oos = perf(P), perf(1 - P)
389	    ins = np.where(np.isnan(ins), -np.inf, ins)
390	    best = np.argmax(ins, axis=1)
391	    oos_best = oos[np.arange(len(P)), best]
392	    ranks = np.array([(np.nan_to_num(oos[i], nan=-np.inf) < oos_best[i]).sum() / (M - 1) if M > 1 else 0.5 for i in range(len(P))])
393	    ranks = np.clip(ranks, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
394	    logit = np.log(ranks / (1 - ranks))
395	    ins_best = ins[np.arange(len(P)), best]
396	    ok = np.isfinite(oos_best) & np.isfinite(ins_best)
397	    slope = float(np.polyfit(ins_best[ok], oos_best[ok], 1)[0]) if ok.sum() > 2 else None
398	    return dict(candidates=M, partitions=int(len(P)), statistic=statistic, pbo=round(float((logit < 0).mean()), 4),
399	                oos_best_below_zero=round(float((oos_best[ok] < 0).mean()), 4) if ok.any() else None,
400	                degradation_slope=round(slope, 4) if slope is not None else None,
401	                is_best_mean=round(float(ins_best[ok].mean()), 2) if ok.any() else None,
402	                oos_best_mean=round(float(oos_best[ok].mean()), 2) if ok.any() else None)

415	def deflated_sharpe(per_session, n_trials, sr_var_trials=None):
416	    """Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014): the probability that the per-session Sharpe of a book is above the expected maximum
417	    Sharpe of n_trials trials with variance sr_var_trials (the variance of Sharpe across the family; estimated from
418	    per_session's own scale when None), with the skew / kurtosis correction. Returns SR, SR0, DSR, p = 1 - DSR."""
419	    x = np.asarray(per_session, dtype=float); T_ = len(x)
420	    if T_ < 3 or x.std(ddof=1) == 0: return dict(sr=None, sr0=None, dsr=None, p=None, T=T_)
421	    sr = float(x.mean() / x.std(ddof=1)); g3 = float(sst.skew(x)); g4 = float(sst.kurtosis(x, fisher=False))
422	    V = sr_var_trials if sr_var_trials is not None else 1.0 / T_
423	    N = max(2, n_trials); em = 0.5772156649
424	    sr0 = math.sqrt(V) * ((1 - em) * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / N) + em * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / (N * math.e)))
425	    den = 1 - g3 * sr + (g4 - 1) / 4 * sr * sr
426	    if den <= 0: return dict(sr=round(sr, 4), sr0=round(sr0, 4), dsr=None, p=None, T=T_, note="denominator <= 0")
427	    z = (sr - sr0) * math.sqrt(T_ - 1) / math.sqrt(den)
428	    dsr = float(sst.norm.cdf(z))
429	    return dict(sr=round(sr, 4), sr0=round(float(sr0), 4), dsr=round(dsr, 4), p=round(1 - dsr, 4), T=T_, n_trials=n_trials, skew=round(g3, 3), kurt=round(g4, 3))

441	    """Politis & Romano stationary bootstrap indices (draws x T_) over T_ ordered sessions; seeded and reproducible."""
442	    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(_sha(f"{seed}|boot|{tag}"), 16) % (2 ** 32))
443	    p = 1.0 / mean_block

446	    idx[:, 0] = starts[:, 0]

479	def spa(vectors, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, tag="", min_active=None, active_tol=SPA_ACTIVE_TOL_INR):
480	    """White's Reality Check and Hansen's SPA over a family of candidates: H0 = no candidate has positive expected selection
481	    gain (per-session kept mean minus the session mean). Stationary bootstrap of sessions, Hansen's consistent recentring;
482	    reported both studentised (Hansen) and unstudentised (White's original statistic, sqrt(T) x mean). A candidate whose
483	    selection gain differs from zero (by more than `active_tol` INR, default SPA_ACTIVE_TOL_INR = 0.01) in fewer than
484	    `min_active` sessions (default max(10, 5% of T)) is excluded from the studentised family: its near-zero variance would give
485	    it an arbitrarily large t (the exit-policy refuter's finding); it stays in the unstudentised family. Gate candidates (keep
486	    masks) are unaffected by the tolerance: their per-session gains are exactly 0 or hundreds of INR. Returns the best
487	    candidate under each statistic and the four p-values."""
488	    Dm = np.array([selection_gain(v)[0] for v in vectors], dtype=float)       # M x T
489	    M, T_ = Dm.shape
490	    if min_active is None: min_active = max(10, int(0.05 * T_))
491	    active = (np.abs(Dm) > active_tol).sum(axis=1)
492	    ok = active >= min_active
493	    mu = Dm.mean(axis=1); sd = Dm.std(axis=1, ddof=1) + 1e-12
494	    idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
495	    mub = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].mean(axis=1) for d in range(draws)])           # draws x M
496	    sdb = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].std(axis=1, ddof=1) for d in range(draws)]) + 1e-12
497	    thr = np.sqrt(np.var(Dm, axis=1, ddof=1) / T_ * 2 * math.log(math.log(T_)))
498	    mu_c = np.where(mu < -thr, mu, 0.0)                                            # Hansen's consistent recentring
499	    out = dict(candidates=M, sessions=T_, draws=draws, min_active_sessions=int(min_active), excluded_from_studentised=int((~ok).sum()))
500	    # unstudentised (White 2000): statistic sqrt(T) x mean gain, every candidate
501	    tu = np.sqrt(T_) * mu; bu = int(np.argmax(tu)); stat_u = float(tu[bu])
502	    rc_u = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu), axis=1); spa_u = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu + mu_c), axis=1)
503	    out.update(best_unstudentised=bu, best_mean_gain_unstudentised=round(float(mu[bu]), 2),

That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.

Expose score(candidate_json, label='L1') as the only way any study obtains a kept-vs-skipped number, so the ledger cannot be bypassed. Add the kept-n floors from decision-making-1 (kept share >= 20%, kept n >= 300 on 1m / 80 on 5m) to the go/no-go so a tiny lucky subset cannot win the kept-vs-skipped statistic. Per-session Sharpe/DSR must use only sessions with a SETUP (579 of 1,026 IS sessions on 1m; the rest are structural zeros). The OOS evaluator is one script, run once, for at most 3 frozen candidates across all 18 studies; every other study's 'OOS once' clause is struck and replaced by 'submit to the harness'. Winsorise the |net| sample weights at the IS 99th percentile before normalising: on 1m the top-decile winners are 46% of gross wins and ~70 rows, so an unwinsorised weight lets a handful of trades set the model. 326	### decision-making-1-fullinfo-bandit-policy-tree-gate (priority 1)
327	
328	**technique.** Offline contextual bandit with full-information rewards, solved as cost-sensitive policy learning: value-maximising depth-limited policy trees (Athey-Wager / Zhou-Athey-Wager) and cost-proportionate weighted gradient boosting, with the policy value computed exactly (direct method, no IPS) and distilled to a rule list
329	
330	**what_it_answers.** Which Foundation SETUPs to take and which to skip, by regime / time / volume / level / card context, chosen to maximise INR value (not accuracy), and whether the learned gate beats the session-matched random gate and the frozen ST7/ST8 gates on kept-vs-skipped expectancy rather than by trading less.
331	
332	**method.** Inputs: fz_v3/minute/setup_features.parquet (5,326 rows, 118 as-of columns) and fz_v3/5minute/features.parquet (1,012 rows, 143 as-of columns). Reward table per SETUP: r_take = fnd_net (primary variant recomputed from bars with a 15:25 square-off on the entry session, stop as hard floor; secondary = the engine's own exit as built), r_skip = 0. Every gate pi has exact value V(pi) = mean(pi(x) * r_take); baselines: Foundation (pi = take), ST7/ST8 (st7_traded / fzpos_kind), session-matched random at the same per-session count. Learners on IS only: (A) exact depth-1 and greedy depth-2/3 policy trees whose split criterion is the policy value (sum of r_take over the take-leaf), min leaf 100 SETUPs (1m) / 40 (5m), implemented in numpy over ~110 features x 30 quantile thresholds; (B) HistGradientBoostingClassifier on y = sign(net) with sample_weight = |net| winsorised at the 1st/99th percentile (Zadrozny-Langford-Abe cost-proportionate reduction; with two arms and full information this is the regret-optimal reduction), policy = take iff P_w(win) > 0.5, plus HistGradientBoostingRegressor on winsorised net with policy take iff E[net|x] > tau, tau swept post hoc from out-of-fold predictions; (C) distillation: fit a depth-<=3 DecisionTreeClassifier (min leaf 100) to (B)'s out-of-fold decisions and extract <= 8 conjunctive rules; report fidelity to (B) and the distilled policy's own CV value. Selection on IS CV only: maximise kept-minus-skipped mean net subject to kept share >= 20% and kept n >= 300 (1m) / 80 (5m); also report the value with the top 1% winners removed (heavy tail: 1m winners median 1.8k, p90 10k INR). Diagnostics: SHAP (TreeExplainer) on (B) for the drivers; winner recall and loser precision; per-hour and per-regime kept share. OOS once: kept n, kept net, skipped net, expectancy difference, winner recall / loser precision, random-control percentile at matched per-session k (2,000 seeded draws), permutation p, calibration of E[net|x] by decile.
333	
334	**leakage_controls.** Features restricted to the README's as-of columns; the ledger's session-so-far fields (today_net_asof etc.) are allowed because they use exits <= k. Excluded by name: fnd_*, fwd_*, fzpos_*, st7_outcome_gate and all st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones.retired_* and visits.end_* unless bar-conditioned. CV = 8 contiguous session blocks (GroupKFold on session_i, blocks kept in time order), purge = drop training SETUPs whose trade exit date falls inside the test block, embargo = 2 sessions after each test block. tau, tree depth, min-leaf and the kept-share floor are fixed above; any change is a new pre-registration. OOS evaluated exactly once with the frozen rule list; the winsorisation and quantile thresholds are computed on the training folds only.
335	
336	**compute.** HistGB on 4.5k x 110: ~2 s per fit; 8 folds x 2 learners x 3 seeds ~ 2 min; exact depth-1 policy search 110 x 30 thresholds trivial, greedy depth-3 ~ 1 min; SHAP seconds; controls (2,000 draws x 1,026 sessions) ~ 1 min. Total < 10 CPU-min per timeframe, peak memory < 400 MB.
337	
338	**libraries.** numpy, pandas, pyarrow, scikit-learn 1.7.2 (HistGradientBoosting, DecisionTree, GroupKFold), shap 0.49.1, numba (optional for the threshold sweep)
339	
340	**output_as_config.** strategy_13.json / strategy_14.json block "gate": {"kind": "rule_list", "default": "take"|"skip", "rules": [{"if": {"reg_n_choch_since_bos": [">=", 2], "hour_bin": ["in", ["11","12"]]}, "then": "skip"}, ...] (<= 8 rules, <= 3 conditions each), "min_expected_net_inr": tau, "provenance": {"source": "learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12", "script": "<name>", "sha": "<sha>", "cv_kept_minus_skipped_inr": ..., "control_pct": ...}}. Every feature named in a rule must be one the lab can compute at the SETUP bar from the card, the engine events and the bars; the GBM never ships.
341	
342	**novelty.** Athey & Wager 2021 (Policy learning with observational data) and Zhou, Athey & Wager 2023 (Offline multi-action policy learning: exact depth-limited policy trees) supply the value-maximising tree; Zadrozny, Langford & Abe 2003 (cost-proportionate example weighting) and Beygelzimer & Langford 2009 (offset tree) are the bandit-to-classification reductions, which become exact here because the reward of both arms is known (Dudik, Langford & Li 2011's doubly-robust estimator collapses to the direct method). Distillation follows Bastani, Kim & Bastani 2018 (policy extraction into decision trees). This differs from H5 in the objective: H5 fits win/loss; this maximises INR value with the skip reward pinned at 0 and the costs inside the reward.
343	
344	**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: Trap: a value-maximising split on heavy-tailed rewards chases the leaf holding the outlier winners (1m p90 winner 10k INR vs median 1.8k), tau 'swept post hoc' on pooled OOF is a selection the ledger must count, and this is study 2's hypothesis run a second time under a different splitter (8 vs 12 blocks), doubling the trials for one question. Fix: keep the 1/99 winsorisation and make the top-1%-removed value a hard pass condition, add a block-wise sign test (kept-vs-skipped > 0 in >= 6 of 8 blocks), log every tau, use the harness splitter, restrict features to study 3's shortlist, and merge with study 2 into one trial family so exactly one gate candidate from the family reaches OOS.
345	
346	**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 4 · keep True — fix: Merge with quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate (same reward, same |net|-weighted HGB); keep the exact depth-limited policy tree as the distinct, most config-native learner. Nest tau: 'tau swept post hoc from out-of-fold predictions' selects on all IS OOF outcomes; choose tau inside each training fold as the meta-label study does. Adopt the harness splitter (12 blocks, 3-session embargo; 3 is justified by the 5m room age and vol_med60 memory, 2 is not) instead of 8 blocks / 2 sessions. Keep the kept-share and kept-n floors and the top-1%-removed value; they belong in the harness go/no-go for everyone. < 10 CPU-min, < 400 MB: runs now.
347	
348	### decision-making-2-exit-policy-fqi-exomdp (priority 2)
349	
350	**technique.** Offline sequential RL for the in-trade exit on an exogenous tape: Fitted Q-Iteration with tree ensembles and a pessimistic (ensemble lower-bound) value, plus hindsight-imitation from the exactly computable optimal exit, evaluated by exact replay (with doubly-robust OPE only where fills are uncertain) and distilled to the lab's position keys
351	
352	**what_it_answers.** How to exit: per bar, hold / exit all / exit one of three lots / move the stop to break-even, as a function of the trade's own path (R so far, MFE/MAE so far, bars held, time to square-off), the card read now, room-edge distances, the regime counters and volume; whether such a policy beats the Foundation next-CHoCH exit and the ST9/ST10 R-ladder on the same entries, and how far it is from the hindsight-optimal exit.
353	
354	**method.** Trajectories: for every Foundation SETUP (IS: 1m 4,502, 5m 832) walk the bars from entry+1 to the entry session's last bar at or before 15:25, with the Foundation stop (prev_swing on 1m, choch_candle on 5m, touch rule, engine fill convention) as a hard floor that ends the episode; this extends the logged trajectory beyond the Foundation exit so that every state has both actions' consequences on the tape (Exo-MDP: the tape does not react to a 65-lot order). State s_t (all as-of bar t): bars_held, unrealised pts / SL distance and / atr14, mfe_R, mae_R, drawdown from MFE in R, session_bar and bars to square-off, atr14, vol_ratio20 at t, card read at t (one-hot from card.csv), room edge ahead/behind in ATR from zones.csv (alive at t), n_choch_since_bos at t and whether a CHoCH against the position has printed since entry (events.csv, i <= t), lots remaining. Actions: start with {hold, exit_all}; if that beats baselines add {exit_one_lot, stop_to_breakeven} with the 3-lot book of ST9 (charges per tranche as the lab does). Reward: realised net per lot on exit (slipped price, lab.trade_charges), 0 while holding; gamma = 1, terminal at exit / stop / square-off. Learner A: FQI (Q_{k+1}(s,a) = r + max_a' Q_k(s',a')) with HistGradientBoostingRegressor on (s, a), 20 iterations, 5 bootstrap Q-functions, act greedily on mean - 1.0 * std (pessimistic value; CQL's support penalty is not needed because both actions' outcomes are observed, but pessimism still guards sparse states). Learner B: hindsight imitation: compute the oracle exit per trade (argmax over t of net_t on the extended trajectory, ties -> earliest), label each state with oracle-exits-now, train a HistGB classifier, policy = exit when P > p* (p* by CV value). Learner C (parametric direct search, replaces the r_combinations grid which was run on 2026 = this study's OOS): stop pts {35,50,75}, scale-out target_r in {1,2,3,4}, trail start/lag in {2,3,4}x{1,2}, time stop in {30,60,120 bars}, exit-on-CHoCH-against on/off; value by exact replay on IS CV. Distillation: fit a depth-<=3 tree to the best learner's decisions on IS states; the shipped policy is the rule set plus C's keys. Evaluation on OOS once, same entries: net per trade for Foundation exit, ST9 ladder, C, distilled A/B, the oracle (upper bound) and a random-exit control (exit at a uniformly drawn bar of the feasible window, 2,000 draws -> percentile); exit regret = oracle - policy; paired session-block sign-flip test of policy - Foundation per trade. DR-OPE (Jiang & Li 2016) is used only as a cross-check for partial-exit fills at limit targets, where the fill assumption (fill at target if touched) is the one non-exogenous element.

content.content:
Structured findings with numbers on IS and OOS separately, the exact definition of every feature and rule, the control percentile for any gate, and a candidate config (JSON) if the hypothesis survives. Adversarial refuters then check leakage, definitions, arithmetic and OOS discipline.

## Addendum (2026-09-29, user instructions after the first launch)

1. **"Ensure to use latest AI and machine-learning techniques to understand the patterns and come up with how to trade in this."** The classical H1-H5 program above is the floor, not the ceiling. A design panel (three lenses: quant-ML canon, sequence/representation learning, decision-making/RL; two judges) selected the modern studies; its output is `DESIGN_PANEL.md` next to this file and is part of the program. The final deliverable is a trading playbook: which Foundation SETUPs to take or skip by regime / time / volume / level context, how to size, how to exit, with out-of-sample evidence and the random control.
2. **"You can use it to figure out the patterns and code in this as well."** Survivors are coded into the lab as new strategies ST13 (1 min) and ST14 (5 min) (`strategies/strategy_13.json`, `strategy_14.json`, reserved and confirmed free with the other sessions on 2026-09-29; list the folder again before creating them). ST5-ST8 stay frozen; nothing in `engine.py` changes; no trading number in code (every threshold, weight file path and learner hyper-parameter is a strategy-file key with a `source`).
3. **"Ensure not to take shortcuts or skip best analysis or modelling or training due to hardware constraint; if that's the call then move to Claude cloud by committing required files."** The four input files are committed under `fz_v3/data/` for that reason. In the cloud: install what the program needs (xgboost, shap, torch, hmmlearn, stumpy, statsmodels, mapie ... as the design calls for), use every core, and run the full grids, bootstraps and training schedules the design specifies; never shrink a model or a resample count to fit a box.
4. **"Even incorporate journal every trade and induce reinforcement learning after each trade to optimize strategy, money management and profit factor."** Two requirements:
   - **Trade journal.** One row per Foundation SETUP (taken or skipped) and per closed trade: timestamp, direction, the full feature vector at the decision bar (card fields, regime, volume, level context, time), the policy's decision and its stated reason, the policy's state id (which model / which update it was made with), fill, exit reason, MFE / MAE, pts, gross, costs, net, R-multiple, and the running book (equity, drawdown, rolling profit factor). This journal is the training set of the online learner and the audit trail of every decision. In the lab build it is a table the strategy writes (`fz_journal.csv` or a `journal` block in the results), never a side effect hidden in code.
   - **Learning after each trade (online / walk-forward).** The policy used at trade t is fitted only on journal rows of trades closed before t (strictly causal; anchored or rolling window as a config key), and is refitted after every closed trade (or every k trades, k a key). Actions: take / skip and position size (lots, bounded by a money-management rule such as fractional Kelly on the calibrated win probability and the expected R, with a maximum lots key and a daily loss stop key). Reward: net P&L per trade with the objective reported as net, profit factor (gross wins / gross losses), max drawdown and the kept-vs-skipped expectancy; because profit factor is not additive, the learner optimises a per-trade surrogate (net, or net with an asymmetric loss penalty) and the policy is *selected* on walk-forward profit factor. Candidate learners, all to be run and compared: contextual bandits with exploration (LinUCB / Thompson sampling on a logistic or tree-embedded model), online gradient-boosted refits, and an offline-RL exit policy (fitted Q-iteration / conservative Q-learning over bar-by-bar in-trade states with doubly-robust off-policy evaluation). Evaluate the whole walk-forward path on IS (learning curve: after how many trades does the policy beat "take everything" and the random control?) and then once on OOS with the learner continuing to update through OOS exactly as it would live. Compare against the static IS-fitted model and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate.
   - The lab strategy that results carries the learner as config (algorithm, features, update cadence, priors, sizing keys, provenance), with a **deterministic, replayable** update path from the journal, so that a rerun over the same tape reproduces the same decisions bit for bit.
5. **"Take all required data to cloud and start from scratch if any compromise has happened in the study here."** The cloud run is the authoritative run and starts from scratch: rebuild both datasets from `fz_v3/data/` with no memory or process limits, rerun every study, and use `fz_v3/built/` (the local build, made under a 1 GB / 2-process limit and interrupted once by a session restart) only as a cross-check of SETUP counts, Foundation trades and the room card — never as an input. Any local number that the cloud rebuild does not reproduce is discarded, and the difference is recorded in `fz_v3/out/QUALITY.md`. Data in the repo: the four futures / spot files only. The options directories (`D:/nifty/data`, `D:/nifty/options`, several GB) are not in the repo, so the cloud runs the futures books (the gate lives on the futures tape); option-type books for ST13/ST14 are produced by the lab on the local machine after the cloud commits are pulled.
6. **Coordination with the other lab session ("Buy only").** Their strategies 19-24 (`rl.py`, `entry_rule rl_v1`) are a contextual bandit (Bayesian linear regression per action, Thompson sampling) that chooses, at each Foundation SETUP, skip or an exit profile x stop x lots from Foundation-side features, with full-information updates in exit-time order, learning from Oct 2021 onward. FZ v3 does not duplicate that: v3 decides take / skip from room, regime, volume, level and time context with its own journal and online learner; for the exit / size stage compose with `rl.py` where it exists (or a config-level reference to it) rather than building a second bandit, and say so in the strategy files. issues.what: The full-design logistic learner (online/full/logts, 108 of 468 rows per timeframe, 'outside the frozen shortlist') is a degenerate fit, not a working learner: the Laplace/Newton logistic on ~305 online-standardised columns with prior precision 1.0 saturates, so p_model is exactly 0 or 1 on 99.7% (minute) / 98.9% (5minute) of SETUPs for k=1 and 99.3% / 92.7% for k=10/300. Consequently the decisions are bit-identical across window (anchored = 300 = 1000), across the net / pf decision heads (W vs 1.5 L is irrelevant when p is 0/1) and across all five Thompson seeds (chol(H^-1) ~ I and |x.w| >> 35): 36 ledger rows share (kept_n 2241, diff 11.08, PF 0.315) on minute, 36 share (428, -477.93, 0.538) on 5minute. FINDINGS prints the seed-spread rows with 'diff sd 0.00' and the family line 'full logts 108 paths, diff > 0 in 108' and puts full/logts rows through the finalist go/no-go (ee3bb53f8c7251b8, 4d0b2708b7798f80) without saying the learner diverged. The 'two linear learners on the full design as a labelled sensitivity' was therefore only performed for lints; the logts sensitivity is untested, not null. This does not change the verdict (no candidate, 0 row-level passes) and the context-design logts is healthy (p_model 0.10-0.21 / 0.18-0.44), so it is a reporting gap, not a false claim of a survivor.

issues.evidence: Reproduced from the journals: minute full__logts__k1__anchored__x head e0.0_s0_net: share of p_model in {<1e-6, >1-1e-6} = 0.99686; decisions identical anchored vs 300 vs 1000 (True/True); net head == pf head == e0.3_s1 head (True/True). 5minute: saturation 0.98910, k10/300 0.92736, same identities. scores.jsonl duplicates: minute (2241, 11.08, 0.315) x36 rows, (2239, 100.82, 0.344) x24, (2240, 101.29, 0.344) x12; 5minute (428, -477.93, 0.538) x36. grep of FINDINGS.md for saturat|degenerat|separab|diverg|identical decision finds nothing.
issues.fix: Add a caveat to FINDINGS.md / findings.json: 'online/full/logts diverged (p saturated 0/1 on >= 93% of rows); its 108 rows per timeframe are ~6 distinct decision vectors and are not evidence about a logistic learner on the full design'. If the sensitivity is wanted, re-run only full/logts with a stronger prior (precision ~ d or chosen by nested evidence) or a step-halved Newton, as new ledger rows counted in the family; do not present the existing rows as a learner outcome.

issues.what: The agent's summary claims 'cumulative kept net > take-all from the first 250-SETUP checkpoint on every path'. On 5minute that holds from 250 for 420 of 468 paths and only from the 500-SETUP checkpoint for 48 paths. FINDINGS section 0 phrases it generically ('beats take-all in cumulative net from the first checkpoint'); the finalist tables (first checkpoint 250) are correct.
issues.where: studies/online_learner/FINDINGS.md line 9 (5minute Result paragraph) and the study's final summary ('learning_curves')
issues.fix: State '420 of 468 paths from the 250 checkpoint, 48 from 500' in the 5minute paragraph; the interpretation (cost avoidance, every skip saves ~1,050 INR) stands.

issues.what: The kept books of the top rows mix the 30 warm-up take-all trades (common to every path; mean -802 INR on minute, -543 on 5minute) with the learner's own takes, and FINDINGS never separates them. The best minute row 19f7ff81224bafa0 (kept 68, PF 1.077) is 30 warm-up trades (sum -24,061) plus 38 learned takes (mean +834, PF 1.495, last take 2022-11-04); the best 5minute row e24ac736ebbfa6d5 (kept 140, PF 0.942) is 30 warm-up plus 110 learned takes (mean +9, PF 1.005, last take 2023-11-06). Every context finalist stops taking anything after 1-2 years, which the learning-curve tables show (kept n flat) but the text does not name. No number is wrong and the row-level floors fail either way; this is an omission that affects how the 'best PF' rows should be read.
issues.evidence: Split of results/minute/journals/context__lints__k1__1000__pf.parquet head e0.3_s1_pf by reason: warm-up 30 takes (mean -802.0), learner 38 takes (mean 834.3, PF 1.495), last take 2022-11-04 09:23; results/5minute/journals/context__logts__k10__300__x.parquet head e0.0_s0_net: warm-up 30 (mean -543.4), learner 110 (mean 9.0, PF 1.005), last take 2023-11-06 09:20.
issues.fix: Add a 'learned takes only' column (n, mean, PF, last take date) to the finalist tables, or state once that every path's first 30 kept trades are the shared warm-up and that the context learners take nothing after 2022-11 (minute) / 2024-03 (5minute).
